title: Land Mutation (Namjari) from Abroad: Step-by-Step Guide for NRBs
metaTitle: Land Mutation (Namjari) from Abroad: NRB Guide
metaDescription: How to complete land mutation (Namjari) in Bangladesh while living abroad: online e-Mutation, documents, fees, hearing, appeal and common problems.
heroIntro: Many NRBs buy or inherit property and then stop after registration or the heirship certificate. Without mutation (Namjari), the government record still shows the old owner, and that opens the door to double sales, tax problems and disputes. This guide is written by Advocate Md. Shah Alam, Supreme Court of Bangladesh, for Bangladeshis living in the UK, USA, UAE, Canada and elsewhere. For case-specific help call or WhatsApp the chamber on 01712655546.

quickAnswer.heading: Mutation in Brief
points: Mutation changes the name in the government land record (Khatian) after sale, gift or inheritance.
You can apply online through the e-Mutation portal; the case goes to the Assistant Commissioner (Land) of the upazila.
Documents: registered deed or heirship certificate, previous Khatian, tax receipts, NID/passport and photographs.
An attorney or family member can follow up; you rarely need to travel unless there is an objection.
If rejected, you can appeal to the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) and then to the Divisional Commissioner.

toc: Can I Do It Without Travelling?

sections.content:
Registration transfers title on paper, but the revenue office keeps a separate record to collect land development tax and to certify possession. Banks, developers and buyers all check the mutation record. If you only have a deed, a later buyer may doubt your possession. See how to check land records online to review your current status.

This article is general legal information, not legal advice. Fees, forms and procedures change; confirm current requirements with the relevant office or a qualified advocate before acting.

• Registered sale deed (or gift deed / heirship certificate with death certificate for inheritance).
  • Previous mutation Khatian and CS/SA/RS/BS Khatian.
  • Land development tax (Dakhila) receipt of the seller.
  • Applicant's NID or passport copy and photograph; for NRBs a passport copy is often accepted.
  • Mouza and plot details: dag number, area, khatian number.
  • Power of Attorney if an attorney applies (see our Power of Attorney guide).

1. Open the official e-Mutation portal and create an account with a phone number.
  2. Select the division, district, upazila, mouza and enter dag and khatian details.
  3. Fill in applicant details and upload scanned documents.
  4. Pay the application fee online through the supported payment method. The official fee is modest; confirm the current amount on the portal.
  5. The Assistant Land Office inspects the documents, may visit the land, and issues a notice to interested persons.
  6. A hearing is held; if there is no objection, the Assistant Commissioner (Land) approves the mutation.
  7. You pay land development tax and receive the new mutation Khatian and Dakhila.

The rules aim for a decision within a defined period, but delays happen. Track the case number regularly through your attorney.

sections.h2: Can I Do It Without Travelling?
sections.content: Mostly yes. The application is online and your representative can attend hearings with a valid Power of Attorney. If an objection is raised, the Assistant Commissioner may want to see you or take evidence. You can also ask to attend via video link or send an affidavit, but this is at the officer's discretion.

• Seller's name does not match the record: first correct the earlier mutation.
  • Inheritance mutation with missing heirs: all heirs must be named; get a correct heirship certificate.
  • Objection by a neighbour or relative: the officer will hear both sides; bring deeds and possession evidence.
  • Area mismatch: request survey or correct in the same application.
  • Delay: follow up through your attorney and, if needed, petition the Deputy Commissioner.

If the Assistant Commissioner (Land) rejects the application, you can appeal to the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) within the time specified in the rules (usually about 30 days), and further to the Divisional Commissioner. For disputes about title, the Civil Court remains available. An advocate can prepare the appeal quickly.

faqs.question: Is mutation compulsory after buying land?
faqs.answer: It is not required to make the sale valid, but it is essential for proving possession, paying tax and selling later.

faqs.question: How much does mutation cost?
faqs.answer: There is a modest official fee payable online. Confirm the current amount on the portal; avoid paying unofficial charges.

faqs.question: Can an NRB apply for mutation online?
faqs.answer: Yes. You or your attorney can apply through the e-Mutation system with scanned documents and passport details.

faqs.question: How long does mutation take?
faqs.answer: The rules set a target period of weeks, but real cases may take longer if there is an objection or missing documents.

faqs.question: What if mutation is cancelled?
faqs.answer: You can appeal to higher revenue officers or file a civil suit for declaration of title.
